title: Round 4 - which cards belong together, and a matrix that reverses everything
focus: Round 4 shifted from ranking single cards to asking which cards belong together, aiming to confirm or reject B2-hold-90 and c14-riskmanaged-wide on genuinely new windows, test four new cards' claimed diversification, and score the combined book from round 3.
headline: Round 3's combined-book finding did not replicate: run unchanged on six windows they had never seen, the same three cards were beaten on every axis by B-momentum alone, because the correlation that made the combination work flipped sign from +0.04 to -0.554.
outcome:
Fourteen cards were run across six entirely new windows with a bull-weighted mean benchmark return, the opposite mix from round 3's bear-weighted eight windows. Round 4's own finding, stated as its section heading, was that round 3's conclusions were properties of round 3's windows rather than of the cards.

B2-hold-90 was not promoted: it lost to its own base, B-momentum, on all three axes, and the take-profit and max-hold-days axis had by this point been tested three separate ways with no version beating the base twice, so the axis was recommended closed.

c14-riskmanaged-wide was not confirmed as a standalone rankable card - its median swung from positive to sharply negative and its worst window collapsed - but its correlation claim replicated and strengthened in the opposite direction its round-3 evidence suggested, so it was kept in the library as a labelled hedging leg only, never again scored on median.

All four cards submitted specifically to be uncorrelated diversifiers failed that test: the two built explicitly for it were the most correlated cards in the field with B-momentum, because analysts had measured daily-return correlation while the scorer used window-level correlation, which is dominated by equity beta rather than trade timing.

A separate, un-pre-registered control arm re-ran the five-card A family, retired earlier on the reasoning that their apparent strength was purely a rising-market artifact. Re-run on round 4's six windows, A-rotation posted a positive median and worst window and beat every surviving candidate, finishing ahead of B-momentum on the composite score - falsifying the specific retirement claim, even though the four A variants remained dominated by their own base on both matrices. The retirement log was amended and A-rotation was reinstated to candidates as a high-exposure comparator.
carries_forward: A-rotation is reinstated to candidates as a high-exposure comparator after the control arm falsified its specific retirement reasoning, and should be carried into round 5.
The take-profit/max-hold-days variant axis (B2-hold-90 and siblings) is recommended closed - three tests across three rounds found no version beating the base twice.

Verdicts about which cards are best or diversify are conditional on the window matrix's regime mix, proven here by the same frozen cards reversing completely between round 3's bear-weighted and round 4's bull-weighted matrices.
c14-riskmanaged-wide should be treated only as a labelled hedge leg going forward, never scored on median as a standalone candidate again.
